questions.question: A company plans to use an Amazon Snowball Edge device to transfer files to the AWS Cloud. Which activities related to a Snowball Edge device are available to the company at no cost?

options.text: Use of the Snowball Edge appliance for a 10-day period

explanation.summary: The 10-day usage period is included in the device rental fee, not considered free of cost.
explanation.why: AWS charges for the Snowball Edge device rental, which includes a standard 10-day onsite usage period. Usage beyond this period incurs additional fees. The free activity does not include the appliance itself or its shipping, which are billed to the customer.

options.text: The transfer of data out of Amazon S3 and to the Snowball Edge appliance

explanation.summary: Data transferred from S3 to Snowball Edge incurs data transfer costs in the AWS billing model.
explanation.why: Uploading data from S3 to a Snowball Edge device is not free. While the device facilitates data movement, outbound S3 data transfer is billed based on volume and region. Customers should consider the associated charges when planning large-scale transfers.

options.text: The transfer of data from the Snowball Edge appliance into Amazon S3

explanation.summary: Importing data from the Snowball Edge into Amazon S3 is included at no additional cost.
keyPoints: AWS includes the data import process from Snowball Edge to S3 in the device service fee
No extra charges are applied for ingesting data once the device is shipped back
Allows efficient large-scale data transfer without paying per GB for the upload
Supports bulk migration of on-premises datasets to S3
examples: A company ships a Snowball Edge with 100 TB of data; upon return, AWS imports it into the target S3 bucket at no additional data transfer cost
explanation.additionalInfo: This model ensures cost efficiency for organizations migrating large datasets. The Snowball Edge device rental fee includes the data import into S3. Only the device rental and shipping are billed separately. This approach allows customers to bypass high network transfer costs for massive uploads.

options.text: Daily use of the Snowball Edge appliance after 10 days

explanation.summary: Usage beyond 10 days incurs additional charges.
explanation.why: The standard rental period covers 10 days; daily usage fees apply beyond this. Therefore, daily use after 10 days is not free.

questions.question: A company has deployed applications on Amazon EC2 instances. The company needs to assess application vulnerabilities and must identify infrastructure deployments that do not meet best practices. Which AWS service can the company use to meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor analyzes resource configurations but does not perform detailed vulnerability assessments.
explanation.why: Trusted Advisor provides guidance on cost optimization, performance, security, and fault tolerance, but it does not scan EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities or security misconfigurations. Vulnerability scanning requires deeper inspection at the operating system and application layer.

explanation.summary: Amazon Inspector assesses application vulnerabilities and checks infrastructure compliance with security best practices.
keyPoints: Automated security assessment service for EC2 and container workloads
Identifies vulnerabilities in operating systems and applications
Evaluates deployment against security benchmarks and best practices
Provides detailed findings and remediation guidance
Integrates with AWS Security Hub for centralized view
examples: Scanning an EC2 instance running a web application to identify CVEs and missing patches
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon Inspector provides continuous and on-demand assessments to help organizations ensure security compliance and reduce risk. It supports CIS benchmarks, network reachability assessments, and common vulnerabilities and exposures (CVE) detection. Inspector findings can be automated for alerting and remediation workflows, making it ideal for organizations needing operationalized security assessments in AWS.

explanation.summary: AWS Config tracks configuration changes but does not scan for vulnerabilities.
explanation.why: AWS Config continuously records and evaluates AWS resource configurations, ensuring compliance with defined rules. It does not provide vulnerability scanning for EC2 instances or application-level assessments. It's ideal for auditing changes and compliance tracking rather than proactive vulnerability detection.

explanation.summary: GuardDuty detects threats based on AWS account activity but does not assess individual application vulnerabilities.
explanation.why: GuardDuty monitors malicious or unauthorized activity using AWS CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs. It identifies compromised instances or unusual behavior but does not evaluate software vulnerabilities or security misconfigurations inside EC2 workloads.

questions.question: A company has a centralized group of users with large file storage requirements that have exceeded the space available on premises. The company wants to extend its file storage capabilities for this group while retaining the performance benefit of sharing content locally. What is the MOST operationally efficient AWS solution for this scenario?

options.text: Create an Amazon S3 bucket for each user. Mount each bucket by using an S3 file system mounting utility.

explanation.summary: Mounting individual S3 buckets per user is not operationally efficient and adds management overhead.
explanation.why: Each bucket would require separate mount configuration, IAM permissions, and network handling. This setup also introduces latency as S3 is object storage, not optimized for local file system semantics. It is not suitable for frequent shared file access among users.

learnMore.title: Mounting S3 as a File System

options.text: Configure and deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Connect each user’s workstation to the file gateway.

explanation.summary: AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway allows seamless local access to cloud-backed S3 storage, providing performance of local caching and centralized management.
keyPoints: File gateway presents an NFS or SMB interface to local users
Caches frequently accessed files on-premises for low-latency access
Automatically stores files in Amazon S3 for scalable, durable cloud storage
Supports centralized management and permissions
Reduces administrative overhead and operational complexity
examples: On-premises team accesses shared files via NFS mount while data is automatically stored in S3
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway is designed for hybrid cloud storage scenarios. It allows users to work with files locally while transparently storing them in S3, providing scalable cloud storage without sacrificing on-premises performance. This approach minimizes the need for managing multiple buckets or complex synchronization scripts, and is ideal for enterprises with high local file access requirements.

options.text: Move each user’s working environment to Amazon WorkSpaces. Set up an Amazon WorkDocs account for each user.

explanation.summary: Using WorkSpaces and WorkDocs provides cloud desktops but may not retain local performance benefits.
explanation.why: WorkSpaces are virtual desktops accessed over the network, introducing latency and complexity. While WorkDocs provides cloud file storage, the solution does not meet the requirement for low-latency, locally shared file access, making it less operationally efficient.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance and attach an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Provisioned IOPS volume. Share the EBS volume directly with the users.

explanation.summary: Directly sharing EBS volumes is operationally complex and not supported for multiple clients.
explanation.why: EBS volumes are designed to attach to a single EC2 instance at a time. Sharing an EBS volume across multiple users requires additional file server configuration and does not scale well. It increases operational overhead and does not provide native cloud durability or integration.

questions.question: According to security best practices, how should an Amazon EC2 instance be given access to an Amazon S3 bucket?

options.text: Hard code an IAM user’s secret key and access key directly in the application, and upload the file.

explanation.summary: Hard coding credentials is insecure and violates AWS best practices.
explanation.why: Embedding IAM user credentials in application code can expose sensitive information if the code is shared or compromised. AWS recommends temporary credentials via IAM roles for EC2 to ensure security and ease of management.

options.text: Store the IAM user’s secret key and access key in a text file on the EC2 instance, read the keys, then upload the file.

explanation.summary: Storing credentials in plain text is insecure.
explanation.why: Plain text credentials can be accessed by anyone with instance access. Using IAM roles avoids storing sensitive information on the instance and enables automatic credential rotation.

learnMore.title: Using IAM Roles for Amazon EC2

options.text: Have the EC2 instance assume a role to obtain the privileges to upload the file.

explanation.summary: Assigning an IAM role to the EC2 instance is the recommended secure method.
keyPoints: IAM roles provide temporary credentials automatically
No need to hard code keys or store them locally
Easier to manage permissions and audit access
Supports automatic credential rotation
Reduces risk of accidental exposure
examples: An EC2 instance uploads files to an S3 bucket using the permissions granted by its assigned IAM role
explanation.additionalInfo: This approach aligns with AWS security best practices, ensuring that EC2 instances have the minimum required permissions via IAM roles. Roles are attached directly to the instance, and AWS automatically provides credentials that expire and refresh, minimizing security risks. This method also simplifies operational management and auditing of access.

questions.question: Which option is a customer responsibility when using Amazon DynamoDB under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model?

explanation.summary: AWS manages physical infrastructure security.
explanation.why: Customers do not manage the data center or physical servers hosting DynamoDB. AWS is responsible for securing facilities, hardware, and network access.

explanation.summary: AWS handles patching of managed services.
explanation.why: DynamoDB is fully managed, and AWS automatically applies necessary patches, ensuring security and availability. Customers do not patch the service.

explanation.summary: Customers control access to data and tables.
keyPoints: Grant or restrict access via IAM policies
Manage table-level permissions
Enforce fine-grained access controls
Audit table access and usage
examples: Using IAM policies to allow a specific user to read from a table but not write
explanation.additionalInfo: While AWS manages the infrastructure and underlying service, customers are responsible for controlling who can access their DynamoDB tables and for configuring permissions appropriately to meet security and compliance requirements.

options.text: Encryption of data at rest in DynamoDB

explanation.summary: AWS provides server-side encryption by default.
explanation.why: Encryption of data at rest in DynamoDB is managed by AWS automatically. Customers can choose encryption keys, but AWS handles encryption mechanics and compliance.

questions.question: Which option is a perspective that includes foundational capabilities of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)?

explanation.summary: Sustainability is not a core CAF perspective.
explanation.why: AWS CAF perspectives focus on business, people, governance, platform, security, operations, and performance. Sustainability is an outcome, not a defined perspective.

explanation.summary: Performance efficiency is one of the pillars in the Well-Architected Framework but not explicitly a CAF perspective.
explanation.why: AWS CAF focuses on organizational and operational capabilities rather than technical performance optimization. Performance efficiency is addressed through design and implementation practices.

explanation.summary: Governance is a foundational AWS CAF perspective.
keyPoints: Establish policies and controls for cloud adoption
Ensure compliance and risk management
Provide accountability for resource usage
Align cloud usage with business objectives
examples: Defining organizational policies for account creation and access control
explanation.additionalInfo: The Governance perspective in AWS CAF focuses on defining controls, policies, and processes to manage cloud resources effectively. It helps organizations ensure compliance, align cloud adoption with business objectives, and monitor usage consistently.

explanation.summary: Reliability is a Well-Architected Framework pillar, not a CAF perspective.
explanation.why: While reliability is critical in cloud adoption, AWS CAF separates organizational and operational perspectives differently. Reliability is addressed in platform and operational practices rather than as a governance perspective.

questions.question: A company is running and managing its own Docker environment on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants an alternative to help manage cluster size, scheduling, and environment maintenance. Which AWS service meets these requirements?

explanation.summary: Lambda is a serverless compute service and does not manage container clusters.
explanation.why: AWS Lambda runs individual functions without managing Docker containers, cluster orchestration, or scheduling. It is event-driven and abstracts infrastructure management, unlike container management services.

explanation.summary: RDS manages databases, not container orchestration.
explanation.why: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service. It provides database provisioning, patching, and backup, but does not handle Docker container scheduling, environment maintenance, or cluster management.

explanation.summary: AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers that manages cluster size, scheduling, and maintenance.
keyPoints: Serverless container management for ECS and EKS
No need to provision or manage EC2 instances
Handles task placement and scaling automatically
Reduces operational overhead
Ensures cluster health and maintenance
examples: Running Docker containers on ECS with Fargate removes the need to manage EC2 instances
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Fargate abstracts away the infrastructure layer for containers. Users define tasks or pods, and Fargate manages provisioning, scaling, and maintenance automatically. This enables companies to focus on application logic without managing clusters.

explanation.summary: Athena is a serverless query service, not a container management platform.
explanation.why: Athena allows SQL queries directly on S3 data but does not manage Docker containers, cluster scheduling, or environment orchestration.

questions.question: A company wants to run a NoSQL database on Amazon EC2 instances. Which task is the responsibility of AWS in this scenario?

options.text: Update the guest operating system of the EC2 instances.

explanation.summary: OS management is the customer’s responsibility when running EC2 instances.
explanation.why: When deploying your own database on EC2, the customer must patch and update the operating system. AWS manages the underlying infrastructure but not the guest OS.

options.text: Maintain high availability at the database layer.

explanation.summary: High availability for databases deployed on EC2 is the customer’s responsibility.
explanation.why: AWS provides the underlying EC2 infrastructure, but managing replication, failover, and high availability for a self-managed database falls on the customer.

learnMore.title: Deploying Highly Available Databases on EC2

options.text: Patch the physical infrastructure that hosts the EC2 instances.

explanation.summary: AWS is responsible for patching and maintaining the physical hardware.
keyPoints: Hardware maintenance and physical server patching
Data center security and infrastructure management
Network hardware maintenance
Power, cooling, and rack management
examples: AWS replaces faulty server hardware without customer intervention
explanation.additionalInfo: Even when customers manage software layers like operating systems and databases, AWS maintains the physical servers and underlying infrastructure. This separation of responsibilities is central to the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, ensuring physical hardware is secure and functional while customers manage their workloads.

explanation.summary: Customers control instance-level security through security groups.
explanation.why: AWS provides the network firewall infrastructure, but configuring security groups for EC2 instances is the customer’s responsibility.

questions.question: Which AWS services or tools can identify rightsizing opportunities for Amazon EC2 instances? (Choose two.)

explanation.summary: AWS Cost Explorer can analyze EC2 usage and provide recommendations for rightsizing.
keyPoints: Visualizes cost and usage data
Identifies underutilized or idle instances
Provides recommendations to optimize instance sizes
Supports filtering by instance type, region, and account
examples: Cost Explorer recommends downgrading a t3.large instance to t3.medium based on 7-day usage patterns
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Cost Explorer enables cost optimization by analyzing historical EC2 usage and identifying instances that can be resized or terminated. It supports exporting reports and automating rightsizing recommendations.

explanation.summary: Billing Conductor manages billing and account structures, not EC2 rightsizing.
explanation.why: It helps organize consolidated billing and custom rate plans but does not analyze resource utilization or provide instance recommendations.

explanation.summary: CodeGuru analyzes code quality, not instance usage.
explanation.why: It provides automated code reviews and profiling for Java and Python applications but does not provide EC2 rightsizing recommendations.

explanation.summary: SageMaker is a machine learning platform, unrelated to EC2 rightsizing.
explanation.why: While SageMaker runs on EC2 under the hood, it does not provide recommendations for resizing unrelated EC2 instances.

explanation.summary: Compute Optimizer analyzes EC2 utilization and provides rightsizing recommendations.
keyPoints: Uses machine learning to recommend optimal instance types
Analyzes CPU, memory, disk, and network metrics
Supports EC2, EBS, Lambda, and Auto Scaling groups
Helps reduce costs and improve performance
examples: Compute Optimizer recommends changing a c5.xlarge to c5.large based on 30-day utilization trends
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Compute Optimizer continuously monitors instance metrics and provides rightsizing suggestions for efficiency. It is complementary to Cost Explorer and provides actionable recommendations for instance resizing.

questions.question: Which of the following are benefits of using AWS Trusted Advisor? (Choose two.)

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor does not manage container orchestration.
explanation.why: Trusted Advisor provides recommendations and best practice guidance for AWS resources, but it does not orchestrate containers or manage workloads.

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor does not manage encryption keys.
explanation.why: Key management is handled by AWS KMS. Trusted Advisor checks compliance and best practices but does not create or rotate keys.

options.text: Detecting underutilized resources to save costs

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor identifies underutilized AWS resources to optimize cost.
keyPoints: Analyzes EC2, EBS, RDS, and other service utilization
Recommends resizing or terminating underused resources
Helps reduce AWS costs
Provides actionable recommendations in the console
examples: Identifying idle EC2 instances that can be stopped or downsized
explanation.additionalInfo: Cost optimization checks in Trusted Advisor help companies identify resources that are not being fully utilized, enabling efficient cost management and governance.

learnMore.title: AWS Trusted Advisor Cost Optimization Checks

options.text: Improving security by proactively monitoring the AWS environment

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor provides security-related best practice checks.
keyPoints: Evaluates IAM usage and access keys
Checks S3 bucket permissions
Assesses security group configurations
Provides recommendations to improve security posture
examples: Identifying S3 buckets that are publicly accessible
explanation.additionalInfo: Security checks in Trusted Advisor enable customers to proactively monitor and mitigate potential vulnerabilities in their AWS environment, ensuring compliance with best practices.

options.text: Implementing enforced tagging across AWS resources

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor does not enforce tagging.
explanation.why: While Trusted Advisor can provide recommendations, actual enforcement of tags is managed via AWS Config or service-specific policies, not Trusted Advisor.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage that users experience when they move on-premises workloads to the AWS Cloud?

options.text: Elimination of expenses for running and maintaining data centers

explanation.summary: Migrating to AWS reduces the need to maintain on-premises infrastructure.
keyPoints: AWS owns and maintains the data center infrastructure
Customers avoid capital expenditures on physical facilities
Operational expenses for power, cooling, and hardware maintenance are eliminated
Resources can be scaled elastically without physical upgrades
examples: A company moves its web servers to EC2 instances, avoiding purchase and maintenance of physical servers
explanation.additionalInfo: One of the key economic advantages of cloud adoption is the removal of on-premises data center expenses, allowing organizations to shift capital and operational costs to scalable, pay-as-you-go AWS services.

options.text: Price discounts that are identical to discounts from hardware providers

explanation.summary: AWS pricing does not match individual hardware vendor discounts.
explanation.why: AWS provides pay-as-you-go and reserved pricing models, but does not guarantee pricing equivalent to hardware purchases. Cost benefits come from scalability and operational efficiency rather than vendor discounts.

options.text: Distribution of all operational controls to AWS

explanation.summary: Customers retain operational control over workloads.
explanation.why: AWS manages the underlying infrastructure, but customers are responsible for configuration, access control, and application management. Not all operational control is shifted.

explanation.summary: Operational expenses are shifted but not eliminated entirely.
explanation.why: AWS reduces certain operational overhead, but customers still pay for service usage and manage operational tasks at the application level.

questions.question: A company wants to manage deployed IT services and govern its infrastructure as code (IaC) templates. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?

explanation.summary: Resource Explorer is for discovery and visualization, not governance of IaC.
explanation.why: It allows searching across resources but does not manage or enforce IaC governance policies.

explanation.summary: Service Catalog enables organizations to create and manage approved portfolios of IT services and IaC templates.
keyPoints: Provision pre-approved AWS resources and templates
Enforce compliance and governance policies
Centralized management of portfolios
Reduce operational risk by restricting non-approved configurations
examples: Providing standardized EC2 and RDS templates to project teams
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Service Catalog allows IT administrators to control which AWS services and infrastructure templates can be used by developers, ensuring adherence to organizational policies and compliance requirements. It provides governance, auditability, and streamlined provisioning.

explanation.summary: Organizations manages multiple accounts and consolidated billing, not IaC governance.
explanation.why: It allows centralized management of AWS accounts and policies but does not directly manage deployment templates or resource provisioning.

explanation.summary: Systems Manager manages operational tasks, not portfolio governance.
explanation.why: It allows patching, configuration, and automation, but does not enforce organizational IaC template governance.

questions.question: Which AWS service or tool helps users visualize, understand, and manage spending and usage over time?

explanation.summary: AWS Organizations manages accounts and policies, not cost analysis.
explanation.why: Organizations allows central management of accounts and policies but does not provide detailed usage visualization or cost optimization recommendations.

explanation.summary: Pricing Calculator estimates costs, but does not track actual usage.
explanation.why: It helps plan and forecast costs before deploying resources, but cannot visualize or analyze historical spending patterns.

explanation.summary: Cost Explorer provides interactive charts and dashboards for tracking AWS costs and usage.
keyPoints: Visualizes historical and current costs
Supports filtering by service, account, region
Provides rightsizing and reservation recommendations
Exportable reports for analysis and planning
examples: Monitoring EC2 usage trends to identify underutilized instances
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Cost Explorer enables organizations to gain insights into their spending patterns and identify opportunities for optimization. It allows visualization of costs over time, forecasting, and cost allocation analysis.

explanation.summary: Service Catalog manages approved resources and templates, not cost analysis.
explanation.why: It provides governance and standardization for resource provisioning but does not track or visualize costs over time.

questions.question: A company is using a central data platform to manage multiple types of data for its customers. The company wants to use AWS services to discover, transform, and visualize the data. Which combination of AWS services should the company use to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

explanation.summary: AWS Glue provides ETL capabilities to discover and transform data.
keyPoints: Serverless ETL service for data discovery, cleaning, and transformation
Integrates with multiple AWS data sources and storage services
Supports data cataloging and schema management
Automates data preparation pipelines
examples: Discovering new datasets in S3 and transforming them into Parquet format for analytics
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Glue enables organizations to prepare and organize data for analytics efficiently, integrating seamlessly with AWS analytics services.

explanation.summary: EFS is a file storage service, not an ETL or visualization service.
explanation.why: While EFS can store data, it does not provide discovery, transformation, or visualization capabilities required in this scenario.

explanation.summary: Redshift is a data warehouse but does not provide data discovery or transformation.
explanation.why: Redshift is optimized for analytics queries and storage of structured data, but does not natively discover or transform raw datasets without ETL tools.

explanation.summary: QuickSight is used to visualize data for analysis.
keyPoints: Provides dashboards and interactive visualizations
Integrates with multiple AWS data sources, including S3, Redshift, and Athena
Supports ML Insights and anomaly detection
Accessible to business users and analysts
examples: Creating visual dashboards for sales and customer metrics from transformed datasets
explanation.additionalInfo: QuickSight allows organizations to derive insights from prepared and curated datasets, complementing ETL processes by providing actionable visual analytics.

explanation.summary: QLDB is a ledger database service and not designed for data transformation or visualization.
explanation.why: It maintains immutable transaction logs but does not provide the ETL or analytics visualization required.

questions.question: A global company wants to migrate its third-party applications to the AWS Cloud. The company wants help from a global team of experts to complete the migration faster and more reliably in accordance with AWS internal best practices. Which AWS service or resource will meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: AWS Support provides technical assistance but does not actively manage migrations.
explanation.why: Support helps troubleshoot and advise but does not deploy or migrate applications on behalf of the customer.

explanation.summary: AWS Professional Services assists with planning and executing complex migrations using AWS best practices.
keyPoints: Provides expert guidance and hands-on assistance
Supports application migration and modernization
Ensures adherence to AWS internal best practices
Reduces time and risk during migration
examples: Collaborating with AWS ProServe to migrate enterprise ERP applications to AWS
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Professional Services offers consulting and hands-on implementation support to accelerate migrations and ensure they are done securely and efficiently according to AWS best practices.

explanation.summary: Launch Wizard helps deploy specific workloads but is not a global consulting service.
explanation.why: It provides guided deployment for supported applications but does not offer expert consulting for migration planning and execution.

explanation.summary: AMS manages AWS accounts but does not provide the global consulting and migration expertise.
explanation.why: AMS is focused on ongoing management and operations, not hands-on migration planning with AWS best practices.

questions.question: An e-learning platform needs to run an application for 2 months each year. The application will be deployed on Amazon EC2 instances. Any application downtime during those 2 months must be avoided. Which EC2 purchasing option will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

explanation.summary: Reserved Instances are more cost-effective for long-term, predictable workloads, not short-term seasonal applications.
explanation.why: RI savings require committing to a 1- or 3-year term. For a 2-month workload, purchasing RI would result in paying for unused capacity the rest of the year.

explanation.summary: Dedicated Hosts provide dedicated physical servers, which is expensive and unnecessary for short-term workloads.
explanation.why: They are intended for compliance or licensing requirements, not cost-effective for seasonal workloads requiring 2 months of uptime.

explanation.summary: Spot Instances are interrupted frequently and not suitable for guaranteed uptime.
explanation.why: Spot pricing is low cost but instances can be reclaimed with short notice, violating the zero-downtime requirement.

explanation.summary: On-Demand Instances provide flexibility and guaranteed availability without upfront commitment, ideal for seasonal workloads.
keyPoints: Pay per hour without long-term commitment
Instances are always available while running
Supports predictable uptime requirements
No upfront cost required
examples: Running the e-learning platform on On-Demand EC2 instances for 2 months each year
explanation.additionalInfo: On-Demand Instances allow organizations to provision compute resources for short-term workloads where uptime is critical, and cost is optimized for the actual usage period. This is more cost-effective than Reserved or Dedicated options for temporary workloads.

questions.question: A developer wants to deploy an application quickly on AWS without manually creating the required resources. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: EC2 requires manual provisioning and configuration of compute resources.
explanation.why: Launching EC2 instances involves selecting instance types, storage, networking, and manually configuring applications, which is not fully automated.

explanation.summary: Elastic Beanstalk automatically provisions required AWS resources for application deployment.
keyPoints: Handles EC2, load balancers, RDS, and other necessary resources
Supports automated deployment and scaling
Reduces manual provisioning effort
Provides monitoring and environment management
examples: Deploying a web application with one click and letting Elastic Beanstalk configure servers, databases, and scaling policies
explanation.additionalInfo: Elastic Beanstalk simplifies application deployment by orchestrating underlying AWS resources automatically. Developers focus on code rather than infrastructure configuration, enabling faster and reliable deployments.

explanation.summary: CodeBuild is a build service and does not automatically provision runtime environments for applications.
explanation.why: It compiles and tests code but does not deploy applications or configure supporting resources automatically.

explanation.summary: Personalize provides machine learning recommendations, not general application deployment.
explanation.why: It is specific to personalization models and does not deploy arbitrary applications or manage compute resources automatically.

questions.question: A company is storing sensitive customer data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to protect the data from accidental deletion or overwriting. Which S3 feature should the company use to meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: Lifecycle rules automate object transitions and expirations, not protection from deletion.
explanation.why: Lifecycle policies manage storage class transitions and object expiration. They do not prevent accidental overwrites or deletions.

explanation.summary: S3 Versioning enables protection against accidental deletion or overwrites by keeping multiple versions of an object.
keyPoints: Retains prior versions of objects
Allows recovery of deleted or overwritten objects
Supports MFA Delete for extra security
Works with lifecycle policies to manage versions
examples: Restoring a previous version of a file that was accidentally deleted
explanation.additionalInfo: Versioning is the recommended AWS S3 feature to protect critical data. By enabling versioning, users can recover from human error, application mistakes, or unintended overwrites, ensuring data integrity and compliance.

explanation.summary: Bucket policies control access permissions, not versioning protection.
explanation.why: While policies can restrict who can delete objects, they do not inherently maintain previous versions for recovery.

explanation.summary: Encryption secures data at rest but does not prevent deletion or overwriting.
explanation.why: Server-side encryption protects confidentiality but does not maintain previous versions or prevent accidental object removal.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides the ability to manage infrastructure as code?

explanation.summary: CodePipeline orchestrates CI/CD pipelines but does not provide IaC management.
explanation.why: It automates build, test, and deployment workflows, but the definition and management of infrastructure resources are handled by IaC services.

explanation.summary: CodeDeploy automates application deployment but does not define infrastructure.
explanation.why: It handles application updates to EC2, Lambda, or on-premises servers, but the infrastructure must be provisioned separately.

explanation.summary: Direct Connect provides dedicated network connectivity, not infrastructure management.
explanation.why: It creates a physical connection between on-premises and AWS, unrelated to defining resources as code.

explanation.summary: CloudFormation enables managing and provisioning AWS infrastructure as code.
keyPoints: Define AWS resources declaratively using templates
Automate creation, updating, and deletion of resources
Supports repeatable and versioned infrastructure deployments
Integrates with CI/CD pipelines for DevOps workflows
examples: Deploying EC2 instances, RDS databases, and VPCs via a single CloudFormation template
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS CloudFormation allows users to manage their AWS infrastructure in a predictable, version-controlled way using JSON or YAML templates. It is central to infrastructure-as-code practices and is often combined with other DevOps services for fully automated deployments.

questions.question: An online gaming company needs to choose a purchasing option to run its Amazon EC2 instances for 1 year. The web traffic is consistent, and any increases in traffic are predictable. The EC2 instances must be online and available without any disruption. Which EC2 instance purchasing option will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

explanation.summary: On-Demand Instances are flexible but more expensive for predictable workloads.
explanation.why: Pay-as-you-go pricing provides no cost advantage when workloads are consistent over a long term; Reserved Instances are more cost-effective for steady usage.

explanation.summary: Reserved Instances provide cost savings for predictable, consistent workloads.
keyPoints: Offer up to 75% savings over On-Demand pricing
Require a 1- or 3-year term commitment
Provide guaranteed capacity
Ideal for applications with predictable traffic
examples: Running EC2 instances for an entire year with stable traffic using Reserved Instances
explanation.additionalInfo: Reserved Instances are optimal for workloads that are consistent and require guaranteed uptime. They reduce costs for long-term usage while ensuring instances are available when needed.

explanation.summary: Spot Instances are low-cost but can be interrupted, unsuitable for guaranteed uptime.
explanation.why: They are reclaimed by AWS when capacity is needed, making them unreliable for critical applications.

explanation.summary: Spot Fleet aggregates Spot Instances but still does not guarantee uninterrupted availability.
explanation.why: It is designed for cost optimization and scalable compute, not guaranteed continuous uptime for predictable workloads.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature allows a user to establish a dedicated network connection between a company’s on-premises data center and the AWS Cloud?

explanation.summary: Direct Connect provides a dedicated physical network connection to AWS.
keyPoints: Bypasses the public internet for lower latency and consistent bandwidth
Supports private connectivity to VPCs and other AWS services
Ideal for hybrid cloud architectures
Improves security by avoiding internet exposure
examples: Establishing a 1 Gbps private link from an on-premises data center to AWS for low-latency database access
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Direct Connect is a service that establishes a dedicated, private network link between on-premises infrastructure and AWS, often used for high-throughput, low-latency, or sensitive workloads.

explanation.summary: VPC peering connects VPCs within AWS but does not connect on-premises data centers.
explanation.why: Peering allows communication between AWS VPCs but cannot provide dedicated on-premises connectivity.

explanation.summary: VPN provides encrypted connections over the internet, not a dedicated physical link.
explanation.why: It is secure but does not offer the low-latency, consistent bandwidth of Direct Connect.

explanation.summary: Route 53 is a DNS service and cannot provide dedicated network connections.
explanation.why: It resolves domain names to IP addresses and manages routing, but does not create private network links between on-premises and AWS.

questions.question: Which option is a physical location of the AWS global infrastructure?

explanation.summary: AWS DataSync is a service, not a physical location.
explanation.why: DataSync moves data between on-premises storage and AWS or between AWS services, but does not represent an AWS Region or physical site.

explanation.summary: AWS Regions are physical locations that host multiple Availability Zones.
keyPoints: Regions consist of multiple data centers (AZs)
Physically isolated to improve fault tolerance
Provide geographic redundancy
Basis for deploying and managing AWS services
examples: Choosing us-east-1 to deploy resources in the eastern US region
explanation.additionalInfo: Regions are distinct geographic areas containing multiple Availability Zones. Each AZ is isolated but connected via low-latency networks. Understanding Regions is critical for high availability, disaster recovery, and compliance.

explanation.summary: Amazon Connect is a contact center service, not a physical location.
explanation.why: It enables cloud-based customer contact operations, but it is deployed within AWS Regions, not a physical site itself.

explanation.summary: AWS Organizations is an account management service, not a physical site.
explanation.why: It manages multiple AWS accounts and policies, but does not correspond to a Region or physical data center.

questions.question: A company wants to protect its AWS Cloud information, systems, and assets while performing risk assessment and mitigation tasks. Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework is supported by these goals?

explanation.summary: Reliability focuses on fault tolerance and operational recovery, not directly risk assessment and mitigation.
explanation.why: The Security pillar specifically addresses protecting information and assets while evaluating risks, rather than system reliability aspects.

explanation.summary: The Security pillar encompasses risk assessment, mitigation, and protection of information and assets.
keyPoints: Protects data, systems, and assets
Enables risk assessment and management
Implements access control and monitoring
Supports compliance and audit requirements
examples: Using IAM policies, GuardDuty alerts, and CloudTrail logs to assess and protect AWS workloads
explanation.additionalInfo: The Security pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework focuses on safeguarding applications and data. It ensures organizations can identify risks, enforce controls, and protect information, systems, and assets effectively.

explanation.summary: Operational excellence focuses on processes and procedures, not directly on risk protection.
explanation.why: While operational excellence ensures efficient operations, it does not directly address security risk assessment and mitigation.

explanation.summary: Performance efficiency addresses optimal use of resources rather than risk management.
explanation.why: It focuses on selecting the right resources and scaling efficiently, not directly on security or risk mitigation.

questions.question: What is the purpose of having an internet gateway within a VPC?

options.text: To create a VPN connection to the VPC

explanation.summary: VPN connections are established using AWS VPN services, not an internet gateway.
explanation.why: Internet gateways provide connectivity to the public internet, whereas VPN connections provide secure private connectivity from on-premises networks.

options.text: To allow communication between the VPC and the internet

explanation.summary: An internet gateway enables instances in a VPC to communicate with the internet.
keyPoints: Provides public IPv4 and IPv6 connectivity
Used for public subnets to allow inbound and outbound traffic
Horizontally scaled and redundant service
Required for NAT Gateway to provide internet access to private subnets
examples: Connecting EC2 instances in a public subnet to download updates from the internet
explanation.additionalInfo: Internet gateways are fully managed AWS components that allow VPC resources to send and receive traffic from the internet. They are a critical component for public-facing services and outbound connectivity from private resources via NAT.

options.text: To impose bandwidth constraints on internet traffic

explanation.summary: Internet gateways do not provide traffic shaping or bandwidth management.
explanation.why: They allow connectivity but do not control throughput. Bandwidth limits must be implemented via other services such as AWS Network Firewall or traffic shaping on instances.

options.text: To load balance traffic from the internet across Amazon EC2 instances

explanation.summary: Load balancing is provided by services like Elastic Load Balancing, not the internet gateway.
explanation.why: Internet gateways only provide connectivity; distributing traffic is the role of ALB/NLB/Gateway Load Balancer.

questions.question: A company is running a monolithic on-premises application that does not scale and is difficult to maintain. The company has a plan to migrate the application to AWS and divide the application into microservices. Which best practice of the AWS Well-Architected Framework is the company following with this plan?

options.text: Integrate functional testing as part of AWS deployment.

explanation.summary: Functional testing is important but not directly related to microservices decomposition.
explanation.why: Testing ensures code quality, but migrating to microservices is about decoupling dependencies for scalability and maintainability, aligning with the reliability and operational excellence pillars.

explanation.summary: Automation supports CI/CD but is not the specific practice of decoupling a monolithic application.
explanation.why: The key practice in this scenario is implementing loosely coupled services, not deployment automation.

options.text: Deploy the application to multiple locations.

explanation.summary: Multi-location deployment supports resilience but does not address monolith decomposition.
explanation.why: High availability involves redundancy, but the question focuses on splitting a monolithic application into microservices for maintainability and scalability.

explanation.summary: Decoupling services is a best practice for scalable and maintainable applications.
keyPoints: Microservices architecture splits monolithic applications into independent services
Reduces interdependencies between components
Facilitates scalability and maintainability
Supports autonomous development and deployment
examples: Migrating a monolithic e-commerce app into independent services for orders, payments, and inventory
explanation.additionalInfo: Implementing loosely coupled dependencies is a core principle of modern application architecture, enabling organizations to improve agility, reliability, and scalability when migrating to AWS.

questions.question: A company has an AWS account. The company wants to audit its password and access key rotation details for compliance purposes. Which AWS service or tool will meet this requirement?

explanation.summary: IAM Access Analyzer identifies resource policies allowing external access but does not report credential rotation.
explanation.why: It analyzes permissions for security risks but does not generate reports on IAM password and access key rotation.

explanation.summary: AWS Artifact provides compliance reports, not detailed credential rotation auditing.
explanation.why: Artifact provides access to AWS compliance documentation but cannot audit IAM credential rotation events.

explanation.summary: IAM credential report provides a comprehensive CSV of IAM users’ passwords, access keys, and their rotation status.
keyPoints: Includes all IAM users in the account
Reports on password and access key age and last usage
Supports auditing and compliance checks
Downloadable for external analysis
examples: Generating the credential report to verify which users have not rotated their keys in the last 90 days
explanation.additionalInfo: The IAM credential report is an essential auditing tool for administrators to maintain compliance and enforce security policies. It allows proactive identification of users with stale credentials and supports automated compliance monitoring.

explanation.summary: Audit Manager helps automate audit processes but does not directly report IAM credential rotation.
explanation.why: Audit Manager can document compliance assessments but for specific credential rotation tracking, the IAM credential report is the precise tool.

questions.question: A company wants to receive a notification when a specific AWS cost threshold is reached. Which AWS services or tools can the company use to meet this requirement? (Choose two.)

explanation.summary: SQS is a message queue service, not designed for cost threshold notifications.
explanation.why: It handles asynchronous message passing but cannot monitor billing or trigger alerts based on cost.

explanation.summary: AWS Budgets allows creating thresholds and sending notifications when cost limits are exceeded.
keyPoints: Set cost or usage budgets per account, service, or linked accounts
Configure email or SNS notifications when thresholds are met
Track actual vs forecasted costs
Supports multiple budget types: cost, usage, RI utilization
examples: Receive an email alert when monthly EC2 costs exceed $500
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Budgets is the primary tool to monitor spending and send proactive alerts. It helps organizations control costs and ensure that financial limits are adhered to.

explanation.summary: Cost Explorer provides usage visualization and analysis but does not actively notify when thresholds are exceeded.
explanation.why: It helps analyze trends and generate reports but cannot trigger alerts automatically for cost limits.

explanation.summary: CloudWatch can monitor AWS billing metrics and trigger alarms for thresholds.
keyPoints: Monitor estimated charges via CloudWatch billing metrics
Create alarms for cost thresholds
Send notifications via SNS or other targets
Integrates with AWS Budgets for proactive monitoring
examples: Trigger an SNS email when the estimated monthly cost for EC2 exceeds $1000
explanation.additionalInfo: By integrating CloudWatch billing metrics with alarms, organizations can receive immediate notifications when costs exceed thresholds, enabling timely action and cost control.

explanation.summary: The Cost and Usage Report provides detailed billing data but does not actively notify when thresholds are crossed.
explanation.why: CUR is for reporting and analytics, not real-time notifications or alerts.

questions.question: Which AWS service or resource provides answers to the most frequently asked security-related questions that AWS receives from its users?

explanation.summary: AWS Artifact provides compliance reports, not FAQ guidance.
explanation.why: Artifact allows access to compliance documentation and agreements but does not answer general security FAQs.

explanation.summary: Amazon Connect is a contact center service and does not provide AWS security FAQs.
explanation.why: It is for customer engagement solutions, not for providing security knowledge or guidance.

explanation.summary: AWS Chatbot enables notifications and interactions with Slack/Chime but is not a FAQ resource.
explanation.why: It integrates AWS services with messaging platforms, but it does not provide structured security FAQs for users.

explanation.summary: AWS Knowledge Center provides answers to frequently asked AWS security questions.
keyPoints: Contains curated answers to common security queries
Supports troubleshooting and best practice guidance
Accessible via web and searchable by topic
Updated regularly to reflect new security information
examples: Looking up how to configure S3 bucket permissions according to best practices
explanation.additionalInfo: The AWS Knowledge Center is the primary resource for users to find answers to frequent questions related to security and other AWS services. It complements documentation, providing practical solutions and guidance based on real-world user issues.

questions.question: Which tasks are customer responsibilities, according to the AWS shared responsibility model? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure the AWS provided security group firewall.

explanation.summary: Customers configure and manage security groups to control access to their resources.
keyPoints: Security group configuration is instance-specific
Determine allowed inbound and outbound traffic
Ensure compliance with internal security policies
Monitor and update rules as needed
examples: Allow HTTPS inbound from 0.0.0.0/0 while restricting SSH access
explanation.additionalInfo: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, network and instance-level security configuration falls to the customer. AWS provides the underlying firewall infrastructure, but the customer must define rules and policies.

options.text: Classify company assets in the AWS Cloud.

explanation.summary: Customers are responsible for classifying and securing their data in AWS.
keyPoints: Identify sensitive and regulated data
Determine access policies based on classification
Implement encryption and access controls as needed
Audit data usage and compliance
examples: Marking S3 buckets containing PII as sensitive and applying strict access policies
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS provides secure infrastructure, but customers must identify and protect their data according to business and regulatory requirements, defining access and governance accordingly.

learnMore.title: AWS Shared Responsibility Model - Data Security

options.text: Determine which Availability Zones to use for Amazon S3 buckets.

explanation.summary: S3 automatically handles availability zones and durability.
explanation.why: Customers cannot select AZs for S3 storage; AWS manages replication across AZs for durability.

explanation.summary: AWS manages patching and upgrades for managed services like DynamoDB.
explanation.why: Customers do not patch DynamoDB; AWS ensures security and availability through managed updates.

options.text: Select Amazon EC2 instances to run AWS Lambda on.

explanation.summary: Lambda abstracts compute management, and customers do not select underlying EC2 instances.
explanation.why: AWS provisions and manages the compute resources for Lambda, removing customer responsibility for EC2 instance selection.

questions.question: Which of the following are pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework? (Choose two.)

explanation.summary: Availability is important but is not an official pillar name in the Well-Architected Framework.
explanation.why: The framework defines pillars as Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, and Cost Optimization. Availability is addressed under Reliability.

explanation.summary: Reliability is one of the five official pillars of the Well-Architected Framework.
keyPoints: Focuses on recovering from failures and availability
Ensures workload resiliency
Designs fault-tolerant architectures
Implements monitoring and automation
examples: Using multiple AZs for database and application redundancy
explanation.additionalInfo: Reliability ensures workloads can operate correctly even in the event of failures and is a core consideration for designing resilient AWS applications.

explanation.summary: Scalability is important but is not a pillar name; it is addressed under Performance Efficiency.
explanation.why: The framework emphasizes efficient resource usage and scaling under the Performance Efficiency pillar, not as a standalone pillar.

explanation.summary: Responsive design is not part of the AWS Well-Architected Framework.
explanation.why: It is a software design approach unrelated to the defined pillars of the framework.

explanation.summary: Operational excellence is one of the five pillars of the Well-Architected Framework.
keyPoints: Focuses on process and operational procedures
Improves deployment and monitoring practices
Supports continuous improvement and automation
Optimizes operations for reliability and efficiency
examples: Implementing CI/CD pipelines and automated monitoring for applications
explanation.additionalInfo: Operational excellence ensures organizations can run and monitor workloads effectively, continuously improve processes, and respond to events with automation and agility.
